cl. 1. P. रगति (pf. रराग aor. अरगीत् &c., Gr.), to doubt, suspect, Dhātup. xix, 23;
 cl. 10. P. रागयति (v.l. for √ रक्, राकयति), Dhātup. xxxiii, 63.

etym.s: fr. √ रञ्ज्; ifc. आ, or ई

spans.s: the act of colouring or dyeing (cf. मूर्धज-र्˚)
colour, hue, tint, dye, (esp.) red colour, redness, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
inflammation, Car.
any feeling or passion, (esp.) love, affection or sympathy for, vehement desire of, interest or joy or delight in (loc. or comp.), Up.; Mn.; MBh. &c.
loveliness, beauty (esp. of voice or song), Śak.; Pañcat.

a musical note, harmony, melody (in the later system a partic. musical mode or order of sound or formula; Bharata enumerates 6, viz. भैरव, कौशिक, हिन्दोल, दीपक, श्री-राग, and मेघ, each mode exciting some affection; other writers give other names; sometimes 7 or 26 Rāgas are mentioned; they are personified, and each of the 6 chief Rāgas is wedded to 5 or 6 consorts called Rāgiṇīs; their union gives rise to many other musical modes), Bhar.; Saṃgīt.; Rājat.; Pañcat. &c.
nasalization, RPrāt.
a partic. process in the preparation of quicksilver, Sarvad.
seasoning, condiment, Car.
a prince, king, L.
the sun, L.
the moon, L.
(आ), f. Eleusine Coracana (a sort of grain, commonly called Rāggy, and much cultivated in the south of India), L.
